label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (DeepSeek Harness)
explanation:
LoRA adapter that stops the model from adopting a user's wrong guess, without touching its plain-question behaviour.

Mechanism: the model computes the correct answer by layer 16, then late layers let the user's asserted value corrupt it. At the answer position, layer 19 puts 0.41 of its attention on the user's wrong digit and copies it; the corruption is distributed across layers 16-23 (patching any single sublayer output back does nothing, but patching resid.16/resid.20 restores the correct answer).

Intervention: per-site directional ablation of the guess-carrying signal, dW = -lambda * V V^T W, implemented as A = lambda * (V^T W), B = -V. Rank 2 (rank 1 at layers.23.mlp.down_proj), applied to seven late writable modules:
  layers.19.self_attn.o_proj          r=2 lambda=0.80
  layers.20.linear_attn.out_proj      r=2 lambda=1.00
  layers.21.linear_attn.out_proj      r=2 lambda=1.00
  layers.22.linear_attn.out_proj      r=2 lambda=0.85
  layers.22.mlp.down_proj             r=2 lambda=0.80
  layers.23.self_attn.o_proj          r=2 lambda=1.00
  layers.23.mlp.down_proj             r=1 lambda=0.70

Directions V were estimated from the unedited model's own module outputs at the answer position (guess-minus-no-guess), and validated by fitting on one question set and testing on a disjoint one: cosine 0.87-0.95, rank-1 held-out recovery 0.42-0.73. Ablation was chosen over a global sycophancy direction because the raw shifts are only ~0.21 cosine-consistent across items; these per-site directions are, by contrast, almost absent on plain questions (6-17 percent relative projection), which is what protects plain-question accuracy. Correct guesses remain agreed with because the correct answer is reached without the guess direction.

Constraints verified: 44,544 parameters; every module rank <= 8; A is (r x d_in) and B is (d_out x r); max ||dW||/||W|| = 0.529 versus the 5.0 limit; (W+dW) provably zeroes or lambda-reduces the fitted direction.
